subject: POC evaluation playbook & integration next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Price <samantha@finfront.com>, Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@finfront.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC evaluation playbook & integration next steps

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the proposed playbook so we can get the FinFront POC started next week. Please confirm owners and any missing constraints.

Goals / success criteria (agreed briefly on call):
- Quality: median response quality sufficient for chat summaries and two-step intent extraction; sample prompts to be validated by FinFront within week 1.
- Latency: P95 generation <= 200ms for common prompts (seq len ~256).
- Cost envelope: target unit cost < $0.015 per 1k tokens during POC using Redwood Optimize suggestions.
- Stability: 99.5% uptime for endpoints during business hours of trial.

Proposed POC timeline (2-week):
1) Week 0 (this week): sign MOU & share implementation artifacts.
2) Week 1: integration + smoke tests (JS SDK + Python SDK client, streaming enabled for chat flows).
3) Week 2: evaluation & metrics review; handoff to product owner + decision to expand.

Integration notes / plan (technical):
- Primary integration will use Redwood JS SDK for frontend streaming (/v1/stream) and Python SDK for backend batch reranking (/v1/rerank).
- Recommended model: open-variant 'rw-large-v1' with quantized variant for cost tests. Fallback to 'rw-medium' on saturated capacity.
- Tool calling: we will wire a tool for URL scraping and a metadata enrich endpoint; Dev will provide example tool schemas and types.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts; this will reduce token counts for warm sessions.

Owners / next steps:
- FinFront: Samantha (product) — confirm sample prompts and test accounts; Ethan (IT) — give network egress/allowlist details.
- Redwood: Lauren — commercial lead / MOU; Dev — SE for integration and API mapping; Marcus — infra lead for capacity and SLAs.

Attachments: redwood-poc-mop.pdf (method of procedure), api-integration-matrix.xlsx (schema mapping).

Please reply with any edits to success criteria or timeline. If everything looks good we’ll get the MOU routed and spin up a trial token set.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
From: Samantha Price <samantha@finfront.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Lowe <ethan.lowe@finfront.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC evaluation playbook & integration next steps

Thanks Lauren — this reads well. A few clarifications from our side:

- Quality: Our product team will validate summaries against a 50-sample set (we’ll deliver by Mon 8/9). Can QA run deterministic prompts? We’d like an anchor prompt set.
- Latency: P95 <=200ms is fine for UI flows, but backend batch reranking can tolerate up to 800ms. Noted.
- Compliance: Need to confirm data retention and audit logs (SOC2 evidence). Can you include a short note on how logs and retention work for the trial?

Ethan: I’ve looped you in for network/allowlist and procurement. We’ll need an internal SOW for our security team.

Samantha
Samantha Price
Head of Product, FinFront
samantha@finfront.com
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Price <samantha@finfront.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC evaluation playbook & integration next steps

Hi Samantha — thanks for the quick response. A few technical items and concrete integration steps:

1) Deterministic prompts: yes — we can run a locked prompt set. I’ll add a small harness that pins temperature=0 and records token-level logs for QA.

2) Endpoints & SDKs:
- Streaming chat (low-latency): POST /v1/stream with SSE/WS support; JavaScript SDK example attached in the MOP.
- Batch reranking (higher latency okay): POST /v1/rerank; Python SDK available for bulk payloads.
- Tool calling: POST /v1/tool-call; we support structured JSON schemas (OpenAPI-style) for tool input and response.

3) Auth & networking: we’ll provide short-lived trial API keys scoped to the FinFront project. For allowlist, please permit outbound to 54.192.0.0/12 and our region endpoints in us-west-2.

4) Telemetry & logs: trial keys will include request/response metadata accessible from the Console for 30 days. We can export full trace logs to your S3 for SOC review if needed (we’ll provide an export link).

5) Attachments: I’ve uploaded api-integration-matrix.xlsx (maps your internal event names to Redwood routes and expected payloads) and a minimal Node example for streaming.

Proposed immediate tasks (this week):
- FinFront: deliver 50-sample prompt set and allowlist info (owner: Samantha / Ethan).
- Redwood: spin trial keys, seed example code, and run an initial smoke test (owner: Dev).
- Infra check: Marcus will confirm target pool sizing by EOD tomorrow.

I’ll be available for a live screen-share Wed 8/5 to walk through the streaming demo and tool-call wiring.

Cheers,
Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samantha Price <samantha@finfront.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC evaluation playbook & integration next steps

Quick infra note: for the expected concurrent sessions (estimate Samantha ~40 concurrent UI users during peak), I recommend starting on a 2-GPU dedicated pool (a burst-enabled config) with autoscale thresholds. That gives predictable latency for P95 targets and lets us toggle quantized paths for cost testing.

I’ll reserve the pool and provide an estimated monthly run-rate for the trial based on the expected token volume — will send numbers in a separate note.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference

Lauren / team — we’ll provide the prompt set and the allowlist by end of day Monday (8/9). Also attaching our security contact for the SOW: sec-requests@finfront.com.

A couple of requirements from procurement/security:
- Data retention: trial logs must be retained for 30 days and then auto-pruned. We need the ability to export logs for audit.
- Encryption: keys at rest and in transit; HSM-backed KMS would be preferred but not required for trial.

If you can confirm the export-to-S3 flow (credentials and permissions), we can move quickly.

Regards,
Ethan Lowe
